kurz: Tomatoes contain a lot of acid, and canned tomatoes often have added citric acid: sweetness, fat and roasted flavours balance it, and a pinch of baking soda neutralises it.
bild_im_kopf: Like a light that is too bright in a room: you can dim it (baking soda) or add warm lamps around it (sugar, fat), and then it no longer glares.
faustregeln: Sugar and carrot cover the [[saeure|acid]], [[natron|baking soda]] removes it: use baking soda only in tiny amounts, too much tastes soapy and makes the sauce flat.
Ketchup brings sugar and umami, but also vinegar: for a very sour sauce, sugar or carrot is the better choice.
Always adjust in small steps and taste: what is in cannot be taken out again.

ursachen.titel: Cooked too briefly, tomato paste not roasted
ursachen.warum: The acid does not cook away. But roasted tomato paste and long simmering add sweetness and roasted flavours that make the acid seem rounder.
fix: Fry the tomato paste in oil until it turns dark red
Simmer the sauce gently for at least 20 to 30 minutes

ursachen.titel: Sour tomatoes or added citric acid
ursachen.warum: Many canned tomatoes contain citric acid (E330) to keep them safe. Underripe tomatoes are also more acidic.
fix: A pinch of sugar, a grated carrot or a little ketchup: they cover the acid with sweetness
Or a knife tip of baking soda per tin: it neutralises the acid and briefly fizzes
When shopping, choose tins without citric acid

ursachen.warum: Fat and salt soften the sharp impression of acid. Without them the acid stands alone in the foreground.
fix: Stir in a knob of butter or a splash of olive oil at the end
Salt and taste again before reaching for sugar

q1.frage: Did you roast tomato paste and simmer the sauce for at least 20 minutes?

q2.frage: Does the tin list citric acid or E330, or were the tomatoes underripe?
